attributes.title: Level 5

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓Did you set the status bar kind to (Hunger) in  [set [statusBar] to] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓ What other kinds can the status bar be set to?  What else might it be used for in a project?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡If the ninja is having trouble adding the Status Bar extension, guide them through the process. Click Extensions at the bottom of the menu, then scroll down to find the status-bar extension (shown below) to add it to the code block menu.
steps.instructions:
Begin the project by testing out the starter code! Use the direction buttons to move the Player sprite across the tilemap, and the A button to send burger projectiles toward the Customer sprite.


Then, add the Status Bar extension to the menu by clicking More then selecting Extensions. Scroll down then select the status-bar extension to add it to the project.


Open Status Bars and drag a [set [statusbar] to] into the [on game update every ms] loop under the Customer sprite blocks. Click on the (Health) bubble and change the status bar kind to (Hunger).


Click ▶ to see a green status bar appear on the screen!

steps.hints: ❓Did you set the [attach (statusbar) to (sprite)] block to (customerSprite)?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓ Why does each Customer sprite need a status bar? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 In this project, each Customer sprite will have a status bar attached to them to show their hunger level. In the later steps, the hunger level will change when they overlap a projectile.
steps.instructions:
The status bar appeared in the middle of the screen! Attach it to each Customer sprite instead.


Open Status Bars and drag an [attach (statusbar) to (sprite)] block into the [on game update every ms] loop. Click on the (mySprite) variable and change it to (customerSprite).


Click ▶ to see status bars attached to each Customer sprite as they move across the tilemap!

steps.hints: ❓Did you select [max] in the [set (statusbar) [value] to] block and set it to pick a random value between 2 and 5?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓ What does it mean to set the status bar [max]? How is it randomly selected?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Point out to the ninja that the [max] represents the highest level of “hunger” that the status bar can be set to. This means that when the status bar is changed (by -1), it will be subtracted from a number randomly selected between 2 and 5. This creates randomness for how many projectiles need to be overlapped by the Customer sprite before it is destroyed.
steps.instructions:
Add randomness to how hungry each Customer sprite is! Set the maximum amount each status bar needs to be full. 


Open Status Bars and drag a [set (statusbar) [value] to] block into the [on game update every ms] loop. Click on [value] and select [max] from the drop down.


Then, place a (pick random) set to “2” and “5” in the parameter.

steps.hints: ❓Did you add a [set (statusbar) fill background] block to the [on game update every ms] loop and select the colors for fill and background?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓ Why might it be important to have two colors in the status bar?

❓ What other colors could you use in the status bar?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Tell the ninja that the [set (statusbar) fill background] block can be read as: “Fill the red background in with green.” This means that the status bar begins as red (at full hunger), and is filled in with green as the sprite overlaps projectiles.
steps.instructions:
Set the color of the status bar and the color that it changes to as it’s filled in!


Open Status Bars and place a [set (statusbar) fill background] block in the [on game update every ms] loop. Change the color in the first bubble to red and the color in the second bubble to green. 


Now, the status bar will start as red, and fill in with green as the sprite’s Hunger level changes.


Click ▶ to see how the status bar color has changed on each Customer sprite!

steps.hints: ❓Did you drag the (otherSprite) bubble into the [change (statusbar) [value] by] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

Ask the ninja:

❓ What happens if you only use the [change (statusbar) [value] by] block? Does it work correctly?

❓ What value is the [change (statusbar) [value] by] block changing?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that the (status bar kind attached to [value]) is important to include, otherwise it causes an error. It’s important to indicate the status bar kind and exact sprite to change the value of, in order for the block to function correctly.
steps.instructions:
Decrease the Customer sprite’s Hunger level each time they receive a burger from the Player sprite!


Open Status Bars and drag a [change (statusbar) [value] by] block into the [on (Food) overlaps (Customer)] container, above the conditional. Type “-1” into the parameter.


Then, open Status Bars again and replace (statusbar) with a (status bar kind attached to sprite) block in the [change (statusbar) [value] by] block. Change the status bar kind to (Hunger) and use an (otherSprite) bubble as the sprite name.


Click ▶ to see the Customer sprite’s Hunger level decrease each time they overlap a burger projectile!

steps.hints: ❓Did you use a [change (statusbar) [value] by] block to replace (statusbar) in the ((statusbar) [value]) block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ What condition needs to be true, in order for a point to be added to the score?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Walk the ninja through the logic of the conditional. If the value of the Hunger status bar attached to the Customer sprite overlapped is equal to 0, then destroy the Customer sprite, change score, and play a sound.
steps.instructions:
Code the Player sprite to earn a point each time they successfully feed a hungry customer!


Open Status Bars and place a ((statusbar) [value]) block into the left parameter of the comparison block in the [on (Food) overlaps (Customer)] container. 


Duplicate the entire (status bar kind attached to sprite) from the [change (statusbar) [value] by] block to replace (statusbar) in the (statusbar) [value]) block.


Now, when the Customer sprite’s Hunger level equals 0, the sprite will be destroyed with a sound, and a point will be added to the score.


Click ▶ to see the Player sprite earn a point when they have sent enough burger projectiles to each Customer sprite!

subgroups.introduction: Create a project that uses status bar extension blocks to change the Hunger level of sprites by sending projectiles toward them.

validationItems.text: Create a status bar that measures Hunger.
Attach the status bar to the Customer sprite.
Set the max number for the status bar to a random number.
Set the status bar to start red and turn green as the status changes.
Change the status bar when a Food projectile overlaps a Customer sprite.
Destroy the Customer sprite if the status bar value equals 0.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 5 of Green Belt! Before you create your final Green Belt project, there are a few neat tricks to learn that could take your game to the next level! Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 5:

badges.title: Extension Explorer
badges.description: Use the scroller and status bar MakeCode extensions to enhance a project.

badges.title: One Direction
badges.description: Set a project’s background to scroll horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.

badges.title: Sticky Tack
badges.description: Prevent a project’s background image from moving unexpectedly.

badges.title: Setting the Bar
badges.description: Create and customize a status bar to be used in a project.

badges.title: Status Symbol
badges.description: Connect a status bar to a specific sprite in a project.
